headline: Funding flows. Budgets stall. Partnerships form.
deck: This week highlights significant funding in satellite manufacturing and defense tech, while budget concerns linger.

stories.head: Cowboy Space raises $275 million for rockets
stories.body: Cowboy Space has secured $275 million to develop rockets featuring orbital data center upper stages, a move that underscores the growing demand for integrated data solutions in space. This funding reflects a broader trend where investors are willing to back companies that promise to merge data with launch capabilities, even if the tech isn't fully baked yet.
stories.soWhat: Investors seem to be betting on the idea that data in orbit is the new gold rush, but the question remains—how many of these projects can actually deliver?

stories.head: Defense budget impasse raises alarms for space
stories.body: The failure to pass a defense budget is drawing attention as a self-inflicted wound in the space race, with implications for funding critical space initiatives. The FY27 budget markup included a $1.4 billion boost for space resilience, but without a finalized budget, the actual allocation remains uncertain, leaving many projects in limbo.
stories.soWhat: In a sector where every dollar counts, this budget gridlock could stall progress and embolden adversaries who are not waiting on Congress.

stories.head: Palantir secures $480M for ground station program
stories.body: Palantir has won a $480 million extension on its TITAN ground station program, further entrenching its role in defense data management. This extension comes as the military increasingly relies on advanced software solutions to manage vast amounts of satellite data, highlighting the growing importance of software in defense strategies.
stories.soWhat: Palantir's ability to secure such significant contracts suggests that software is becoming the backbone of modern military operations, even as hardware struggles to keep pace.

watchlist.title: Creotech's satellite factory funding efforts
watchlist.body: Creotech is looking to raise $118 million for a new satellite factory in Poland, which could influence European satellite manufacturing dynamics.

watchlist.title: Anduril and L3Harris collaboration
watchlist.body: The partnership between Anduril and L3Harris for a tactical SDA constellation bid could reshape defense satellite strategies.

watchlist.title: True Anomaly's Series C implications
watchlist.body: True Anomaly's $190 million Series C funding may signal increased interest in co-orbital security solutions from the Defense Department.

watchlist.title: Astranis' strategic funding for comms
watchlist.body: Astranis' $250 million strategic funding round might accelerate its microGEO production, impacting the small satellite communications market.

talent.statLabel: Week-over-week growth in resumes from primes to Series B/C
talent.head: Talent is leaving big-aero — and it's not about money
talent.body: Compensation is not the gating factor. The complaint, almost universally, is schedule risk — the inability to ship anything quickly, the half-decade gap between joining and seeing flight hardware, the meeting that exists to schedule the meeting. The startups absorbing this talent will, in two years, be hard to compete with on a level playing field.
